title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code's effective distance below threshold
authors: César Hernando de la Fuente, Joonas Majaniemi, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Felix Frohnert
abstract: Correlated decoding improves matching and clustering surface-code decoders by reweighting one decoding subgraph conditioned on the other's correction. We show that standard reweighting can cause correlated decoders to fail on size-$(d-1)/2$ fault configurations that a distance-$d$ code should correct, reducing error suppression deep below threshold. Under circuit-level noise, a single first-pass edge can discount several correlated edges, even though their joint occurrence requires additional independent faults, so the decoder favors an over-discounted correction. Regularizing the reweighting rule restores the nominal distance scaling and a clear correlated-decoding advantage.
summary: This paper investigates why advanced correlated decoding methods for surface codes lose their expected error suppression scaling when the physical error rate is very low. The authors demonstrate that the standard reweighting rule causes an artificial discounting of error costs. By introducing a specific, error-rate-dependent regularization parameter, they successfully restore the theoretical distance scaling, significantly improving the reliability of the quantum memory circuit.
main_problem: Standard correlated decoding techniques for surface codes fail to maintain the expected effective distance scaling below the fault-tolerance threshold ($p 	o 0$).
main_result: Introducing an error-rate-dependent regularization parameter restores the nominal distance scaling and preserves the advantage of correlated decoding deep below threshold.
method: The authors analyze the logical error probability scaling by comparing standard correlated decoding (CM/LCD) against an optimally regularized version (RCM/RC-LCD).
model_or_system: The study uses the surface code quantum memory circuit simulated under the SI1000 noise model, characterized by a two-qubit depolarizing error probability $p$.
key_observables: Logical error probability ($P_L$) vs. physical error rate ($p$); the effective code distance, characterized by the scaling exponent of $P_L$.
important_parameters: Code distance ($d$), physical error rate ($p$), and the regularization strength ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The failure is localized to the reweighting protocol, not the underlying decoders; the analysis is performed under the SI1000 noise model.
figures_summary: Figures compare $P_L$ vs. $p$ for standard vs. regularized decoders, showing the recovery of expected scaling. Other figures analyze weight distributions and fault contributions.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the failure of standard correlated decoding at low $p$ by showing incorrect scaling. It then mathematically derives the failure mechanism related to weight discounting and proposes a regularization term $\alpha^*(p)$ to correct this, demonstrating its success in restoring theoretical scaling.
why_interesting: The work provides a concrete, mathematically derived method (regularization) to improve the performance of quantum error correction codes in the deep sub-threshold regime, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

FIG. 4. Probability-weighted contributions to PL from fixed-size errors. Results are shown for rotated planar code memory simulations under SI1000 noise with r = d syndrome-extraction rounds and code distances d = {3, 5, 7}. We evaluate contributions from configurations containing exactly t = (d−1)/2 faults (squares) and t+1 = (d+1)/2 faults (triangles), resolved for matching, correlated matching (CM), and regularized correlated matching (RCM). Persistence of the t-fault contribution toward low p diagnoses a loss of the nominal distance scaling. Standard CM generates such a contribution, while RCM suppresses it.

FIG. 6. Ratio of logical error probabilities for stan- dard and regularized correlated matching with re- spect to uncorrelated MWPM under uniform depo- larizing noise. Open markers denote the standard update, α = 1, and filled markers the regularized update with α∗(p). Dashed curves show fits of the form 1 + a + bp + c/p, and solid curves fits of the form 1 + a + bp. The horizontal line marks equal performance. As p →0, the standard correlated decoder degrades relative to the uncorrelated decoder, while regularization restores a correlated decoding advantage across the error rates studied.
